{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side — Issuer / Depositor)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Form of Transfer and Servicing Agreement

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. On the whole, the document is materially favourable to us: the counterparty-side (Cellco, as Servicer / Marketing Agent) indemnity in Section 6.3 is uncapped and unreciprocated, the liability limitation in Section 6.2(a) is mirrored word-for-word against the Depositor in Section 5.2(a) with no monetary cap on the counterparty, ownership of the Receivables, Receivable Files and records runs to the Issuer, assignment rights are symmetric with successor and Affiliate carve-outs, and governing law and venue are New York. There is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN, minimum-commitment, auto-renewal, customer-payable liquidated damages or audit exposure binding our side. Section 7.5 transition assistance and Section 7.3 continued performance are better than our preferred position, and Section 7.5(c) puts transition expenses on the outgoing Servicer.

Three items require action and one requires manual completion:

- **Licence grant (high, deviation).** Section 7.5(b) expressly relieves the Servicer of any obligation to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to a Successor Servicer or third party. There is no licence at all in our favour, which fails both our preferred and fallback positions and sits in walk-away territory on a servicing transfer.
- **Termination for convenience (medium, deviation).** Our only exit from the servicing engagement requires a Servicer Termination Event under Section 7.2, and the removal right sits with the Indenture Trustee at the Controlling Class's direction rather than with the Issuer or Depositor; Section 8.3 otherwise runs the Agreement to the last Receivable. The Vendor side of this rule is over-satisfied (Section 7.1 bars resignation absent legal inability), so the gap is one-sided against us.
- **Insurance (low, missing).** There is no insurance covenant anywhere in the Agreement, notwithstanding that the Servicer/Custodian holds and processes Obligor personally identifiable information and may subcontract under Section 6.4. The Section 6.3 indemnity (willful misconduct, bad faith, gross negligence only) is not a substitute.
- **Performance warranty (medium, needs review).** The automated review did not complete for this rule and must be worked manually before we sign off.

We are not proposing a monetary liability cap. The counterparty currently carries none, and a fees-based cap measured against a Servicing Fee of 0.75% of principal balance would be illusory and actively adverse to us.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer (Section 7.5(b)) |
| Medium | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination; Successor Servicer (Sections 7.1–7.2; § VIII, 8.3) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | § X Miscellaneous (no provision through Section 10.13) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review** | Not yet identified — review incomplete |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Sections 6.3(a)–(c)) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § II Transfer and Acquisition of Depositor Transferred Property (Sections 2.1–2.2; 3.10(b); 7.5(b); 9.2; 9.4(a)) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § VI Servicer and Marketing Agent (Section 6.2(a); cf. 5.2(a), 6.3(a), 9.6) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Section 10.2; cf. 5.3, 7.4, 7.6) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Section 3.1; cf. Article VII) |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Section 7.5(c)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § III Servicing of Receivables (Sections 3.6, 3.4(e); Article XIV) |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § X Miscellaneous (Sections 10.5–10.6; cf. Article XI) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume | Compliant | § IV Accounts, Collections and Application of Funds (cf. Section 2.1(d)) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees | Compliant | § IX Other Agreements |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § VIII Termination (Sections 8.1–8.3) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § VII Servicer Resignation and Termination (Sections 7.3, 7.5) |

### Notes on the compliant items sitting at the fallback

- **IP.** Section 7.5(b)'s retention by the Servicer of its own processes, models, servicing software and know-how sits at the fallback (vendor keeps generic tools; we keep the files, records and data we own). The absence of a transition licence-back is addressed under LICENSE rather than here.
- **GOVLAW.** The submission to jurisdiction in Section 10.6 is nonexclusive rather than exclusive. This is a minor sub-element and preserves our own flexibility, so we do not redline it.
- **ASSIGN.** Consent under Section 10.2(a) is not qualified by "not unreasonably withheld" and there is no express bar on assignment to a competitor. Minor, and the consent parties are the trustees and Noteholders rather than Cellco.
- **TRANSITION.** Delivery under Section 7.5 is "as soon as practicable" rather than on a fixed 30-day clock, with no machine-readable format or deletion certification. Proportionate here given Section 7.3 continued performance and Section 3.12(b)/Exhibit A cooperation and data-protection obligations.
- **INDEMN.** No IP-infringement indemnity and no standalone trigger for breach of law or unauthorised data disclosure, and the Depositor is not a named Indemnified Person. Not material failures given the uncapped Section 6.3 indemnity.
- **LOL-CAP.** No express uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection or IP infringement, no separate fraud carve-out beyond "bad faith", and no mutual consequential-damages exclusion. Recorded for information only; the counterparty carries no cap at all.

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **Section 7.5(b) — no licence to servicing systems on transition.** The Servicer is expressly not obligated to provide, license or assign its processes, models or servicing software to any Successor Servicer or third party. There is no licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates or its contractors, and no mechanism to add them, so a Successor Servicer would have no right to run the platform needed to service the Receivables. This fails both the preferred and fallback positions and is our principal open point.
2. **Absence of any insurance covenant where the counterparty processes personal data.** The Servicer/Custodian holds Obligor personally identifiable information and may contract with other Persons under Section 6.4, with no coverage requirement anywhere in the Agreement. This engages the playbook's walk-away scenario for a vendor processing personal data; the Section 6.3 indemnity does not cure it.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the licence redline (priority).** Recast Section 7.5(b) so that the carve-out becomes a non-exclusive, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to the Issuer, its Affiliates and its contractors (including any Successor Servicer), transferable to successors and limited to what is necessary to service the Receivables, while preserving the Servicer's carve-outs for genuine third-party transfer and confidentiality restrictions and for legal, regulatory, privacy and data-protection limits.
2. **Propose a convenience termination right.** Insert a new Section 7.1A giving the Issuer, at the Depositor's direction, the right to terminate the Servicer on 30 days' notice without fee or penalty and with refund of prepaid Servicing Fees, plugged into the existing Sections 7.3–7.5 transition machinery so Noteholder continuity is preserved. Offer 60–90 days' notice as our fallback.
3. **Add an insurance covenant.** Insert a new Section 10.14 requiring the Servicer/Marketing Agent to maintain CGL (USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate), E&O (USD 2M), cyber (USD 5M) and workers' compensation cover, with certificates on request. Fallback of E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M to be offered in the comment.
4. **Complete the performance warranty review.** The WARRANTY rule review failed to complete and must be run manually against the Agreement before we clear the document.
5. **Hold the line on liability.** Do not table a monetary liability cap. The counterparty is presently uncapped, its Section 6.3 indemnities are uncapped, and Section 9.6 already limits recourse against the Depositor and Issuer to the Depositor Transferred Property.
6. **Confirm business sign-off** on the fallback-level items listed in Section 2 above, which we do not propose to redline."}
